Security Incident Response Runbook

What to do when something may have compromised Acme Digital or client data, accounts or devices. Owner: Nicolás Ferraro (IT and Security). If you are not sure whether it is an incident, report it anyway: a false alarm costs minutes, a late report can cost a client.

Severity levels

SeverityTypical cases
SEV1 — CriticalConfirmed exposure of client or customer personal data, takeover of a client ad account or social profile, ransomware on any device
SEV2 — HighSuspected compromise of a single account, phishing where someone entered credentials, loss of an unencrypted device with client files
SEV3 — LowPhishing reported with no clicks, lost device with full-disk encryption and remote wipe, malware blocked by the antivirus

Who to page

  • SEV1: page the IT on-call phone (+54 11 5555-0199) and Nicolás Ferraro directly. He brings in Martín Arrieta (COO) and Valeria Quiroga (CEO) within the first hour, and the account lead of every affected client joins the incident channel.
  • SEV2: call the IT on-call phone and post in #it-seguridad; the account lead of the affected client is informed.
  • SEV3: open a ticket at it@acme.example or post in #it-seguridad; IT picks it up the next business day.

Never report an incident only in a group chat or by email to a single person: if nobody acknowledges within the target time, call the on-call phone again.

SeverityAcknowledgeContainNotify affected clientsPost-mortem
SEV115 minutes, 24/7Within 4 hoursWithin 24 hours of confirmationWithin 5 business days
SEV21 hour, 24/7Within 24 hoursWithin 48 hours, if client data or accounts are involvedWithin 10 business days
SEV3Next business dayWithin 5 business daysNot requiredNot required (log only)

Evidence preservation

  • Do not wipe, reimage or factory-reset a device before IT says so; disconnect it from the network and leave it powered on.
  • Export the relevant logs right away: Google Workspace audit log, Meta Business Suite and Google Ads change history, Litware Vault access log.
  • Take timestamped screenshots and keep the original phishing email as an attachment, not forwarded inline.
  • Store everything in a restricted Drive folder named IR-YYYY-NN (for example IR-2026-07) and keep it for 2 years.
  • Log every action in the incident timeline document with the time (UTC-3) and the name of the person who did it.

Communication templates

Internal update, posted in the incident Slack channel:

SEV[n] declared at [time]. Incident lead: [name]. Affected: [systems or clients]. Next update at [time]. Do not discuss this outside this channel.

Client notification, sent by the account lead from their acme.example address after review by Nicolás Ferraro and Martín Arrieta:

We detected [what] on [date] affecting [scope]. We have already [containment steps] and will send the next update by [time]. Your contact for this incident is [name and email].

Do not speculate about causes or blame in any message. Only the CEO speaks to the press.

Post-mortem

Every SEV1 and SEV2 gets a blameless post-mortem led by Nicolás Ferraro, with summary, timeline, root cause, impact, what went well and action items with owners and due dates. It is shared with leadership, and a client version is sent when the client asks for it. Action items are tracked in Notion and reviewed at the monthly IT meeting until closed.
